XXI.}}}}</noinclude>into Syria, and came to Tyre: for there the {{ls}}hip vvas to di{{ls}}charge her lode. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=4}} And finding di{{ls}}ciples, vve taried there {{ls}}euen daies: vvho {{ls}}aid to Paul by the Spirit, that he {{ls}}hould not goe vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=5}} And the daies being expired, departing vve went forvvard, al bringing vs on the vvay, vvith their vviues and children, til vve vvere out of the citie: and falling vpon our knees on the {{ls}}hore, vve praied. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=6}} And vvhen vve had bid one an other farevvel, vve vvent vp into the {{ls}}hip: and they returned vnto their owne.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=7}} But we hauing ended the nauigation, from Tyre came dovvne to Ptolomáis: and {{ls}}aluting the brethren, vve taried one day with them.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=8}} And the next day departing, vve came to Cæ{{ls}}aréa.

Philip being Deacon.}}∷ foure daughters {{sup|‖}} virgins, that did prophecie. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=10}} And as we abode there for certaine daies, there came a certaine prophet from Ievvrie, named Agabus. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=11}} He, when he was come to vs, tooke Paules girdle: and binding his owne handes & feete, he {{ls}}aid, Thus {{ls}}aith the holy Gho{{ls}}t: The man who{{ls}}e girdle this is, {{ls}}o {{ls}}hal the Iewes binde in Hieru{{ls}}alem, & {{ls}}hal deliuer him into the handes of the Gentiles. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=12}} Which when vve had heard, vve & they that vvere of the {{ls}}ame place, de{{ls}}ired him that he would not goe vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=13}} Then Paul an{{ls}}vvered, and {{ls}}aid, What doe you, vveeping and afflicting my hart? for I am ready not only to be bound, but to die al{{ls}}o in Hieru{{ls}}alem for the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=14}} And vvhen vve could not per{{ls}}uade him, we cea{{ls}}ed, {{ls}}aying, The vvil of our Lord be done.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=15}} And after the{{ls}}e daies, being prepared, vve vvent vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=16}} And there came al{{ls}}o of the di{{ls}}ciples from Cæ{{ls}}aréa vvith vs, bringing with them one Ia{{ls}}on a Cyprian (vvith vvhom vve {{ls}}hould lodge) an old di{{ls}}ciple. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=17}} And when vve vvere come to Hieru{{ls}}alem, the brethren receiued vs gladly. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=18}} And the day folovving Paul vvent in vvith vs to Iames, and al the Auncients vvere a{{ls}}{{ls}}embled. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=19}} Vvhom vvhen he had {{ls}}aluted, he told particularly vvhat God had done among the Gentiles by his mini{{ls}}terie. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=20}} But they hearing it, magnified God, and {{ls}}aid to him: Thou {{ls}}ee{{ls}}t (brother) how many thou{{ls}}ands there are among the Ievves that haue beleeued: and al are zelátours of the Lavv. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=21}} But they haue heard of thee that thou doe{{ls}}t teach tho{{ls}}e Iewes<noinclude>{{continues|that}}</noinclude>
